summary: Platts: SE Asia PP +USD 50 w/w (yarn/inj 1,360 CFR, BOPP 1,380, block copo 1,410); China feedstock-driven
Jinneng/Petrochina +40-45 to 1,440-1,460 CIF; Korea lower in small volume (Lotte homo 1,360)
Domestic lifted but below imports: NSRP 114G 40,000, BSR T3034 pushed to 41,000; buyers wait on China
paras: Platts (Oct 16): in Northeast Asia, PP yarn/injection rose a strong USD 50/tonne this week, while BOPP, IPP Film and block copolymer jumped USD 100-110. In Southeast Asia all PP grades rose USD 50 w/w — PP yarn/inj to 1,360 CFR, BOPP 1,380, IPP Film 1,460, block copo 1,410.

Asian PP climbed on rising feedstock costs and upstream gains. In China, shortages of naphtha and propane drove prices up; thin margins cut PP operating rates from 70% to 65%. Still, Chinese producers' inventories have risen as buying stalled after buyers resisted overly steep hikes. High ocean freight has made exports to Europe and South America unviable, limiting flows even to Southeast Asia.

In Southeast Asia PP rose mainly because Chinese exporters raised offers, while substitute supply from Korea and the Middle East stayed limited. In Vietnam, some market participants said high prices have led many processors to stop buying on 3-month contracts and instead buy only after confirmed end-customer orders; domestic supply remains stable and few hold large inventories, expecting prices to fall.

Mid-week, Jinneng and Petrochina (China) PP yarn/inj/BOPP offers to Vietnam rose sharply USD 40-45 to 1,440-1,460 CIF; PP copo ~1,480-1,490 CIF; ZPC PP homo recorded at 1,510 CIF. Korean material was quoted lower but in small volume: UPP & H&L Advanced PP homo 1,400 CIF, BOPP 1,420, block copo 1,450-1,480; Lotte PP homo 1,360 CIF.

Domestically, after timid adjustments early in the week, offers were raised more clearly yesterday though still well below new import levels. In the north, NSRP distributor Kanetorra lifted PP 114G to VND 40,000/kg incl VAT; domestic & Korean/Chinese PP yarn/inj to 40,200-40,500; Chinese copo K8003/K8009 at 40,500-41,000.

In the south, BSR PP yarn T3034 was pushed up to VND 41,000/kg incl VAT, above northern quotes; some Chinese PP yarn/inj to 40,700-41,200. Hyosung Vina held PP injection J700N at VND 39,600/kg excl VAT (~42,770 with VAT) and PP random R801N at 41,200 excl VAT (~44,500 with VAT).
Chemdo quoted Chinese PP copo 36MK10 at VND 42,800/kg incl VAT (north) and 43,300 (south), both freight-included for late-Oct/early-Nov delivery — levels seen as high relative to buyers' acceptance.

summary: Small Mid-East/Russian cargoes due, mainly for prior orders; China supply thin, many delays
LDPE lifted again (260GG 46.5-47k, PTT 2426K 48-48.5k); LLDPE flat-to-up, HDPE easing (LSP 5502B -200)
Imports: Petrochina LLDPE +50 to 1,450-1,460; Lotte Titan settled LDPE 1,580-1,600; PTT +10 to 1,430
paras: ThitruongHatnhua.com (Oct 16): some Middle Eastern PE cargoes (incl. Sabic Saudi LLDPE Film) are due at Hai Phong next week, in small volumes mainly to fulfil prior confirmed orders — e.g. Sabic LLDPE 218WJ quoted at VND 42,000/kg incl VAT, Hai Phong next week. Some Russian-origin PE (mostly HDPE) contracted 2-3 months ago is also arriving in scattered lots, only for closed orders.
China remains the largest PE source into Vietnam though weekly arrivals are thin and many orders delayed, so prompt domestic supply is improving only slowly despite abundant import offers.

Mid-week, some traders lifted LDPE again: north LDPE Film 260GG (Lotte Titan) to VND 46,500-47,000; PTT Thai LDPE 2426K/2426H jumped to 48,000-48,500 (little trader stock; PTT not offering Oct-Nov to Vietnam); Korean/Mid-East LDPE Film flat-to-slightly-up at 45,000-46,000.

For LLDPE, after a strong early-week rise, mid-week offers held flat or edged up on scarce grades, with wide seller spreads. Mid-East LLDPE Film held high at VND 43,500-44,000; Chinese-origin LLDPE Film ~41,500-42,000.

For HDPE, LSP offered CP Chem Singapore HDPE blow 5502B at VND 43,200/kg incl VAT (-200 w/w), retail 42,600-42,800 — above Chinese/US HDPE blow (39,700-40,000) and Mid-East 5502BN (41,300-41,500); HDPE Film 39,500-42,000, down w/w.

On imports, Petrochina LLDPE Film +USD 50 to 1,450-1,460 CIF Hai Phong; Lotte Titan settled LDPE Film/Shrink 1,580-1,600 CIF, LDPE coating 800YY & LLDPE injection 300YY at 1,680. PTT Thai LLDPE inj & HDPE Film/yarn +USD 10 to 1,430 CIF HCMC. Formosa HDPE yarn 1,380, LLDPE inj 1,430-1,440. Basell LDPE Film 2427K/2427H 1,530 CIF HCMC (ETD Nov); Equate Kuwait LLDPE Film 7087 at 1,385 CIF.

Platts (regional): NE Asia HDPE +USD 40, LLDPE +45, LDPE +50 w/w. SE Asia HDPE +20 to 1,290-1,300 CFR, LLDPE +20 to 1,240, mLLDPE C6 +20 to 1,390, LDPE +20 to 1,610. PE rose across Asia, led by China post-holiday; smaller gains in SE Asia/Vietnam amid quiet trade, on high crude/naphtha and tight LDPE supply.

summary: Formosa 2nd Oct revision: S65 +10 (China 870, SE Asia 900, India 1,000 CFR); India spread >USD 100
Platts: China PVC 855 CFR / SE Asia 825 flat; oil-based FOB China +5 to 755, coal 730 flat
SCG early Nov quotes (SG660 845, SP660 840 CIF); domestic 23,700-24,200; Yihua SG-5 23,100 Yen Vien
paras: ThitruongHatnhua.com (Oct 16): Taiwan's Formosa issued a 2nd revision to its October-cargo PVC offers — PVC S65 to China +USD 10 to 870 CFR, to Southeast Asia (incl. Vietnam) +10 to 900, to India +25 to 1,000 CFR.
Re-pricing October cargoes mid-month signals slow allocation and high input-cost pressure. The India-vs-China/SE-Asia PVC spread has widened to over USD 100/tonne, the highest in months.

Platts (regional): China PVC held at USD 855 CFR w/w; Southeast Asia flat at 825 CFR; across Asia prices held flat (SE Asia range 810-850 CFR). Buyers in SE Asia largely stay on the sidelines awaiting November offers; weak downstream demand and expectations of further falls limit prompt buying.
Oil-based PVC export quotes FOB China edged up USD 5 to 755 FOB; coal-based held at 730 FOB. High ocean freight means CIF Vietnam can run up to USD 50 above FOB.

In Vietnam, SCG Thailand offered November-delivery PVC (among the earliest regional Nov quotes): SG660 at 845 CIF, SP660 at 840 CIF, barely 1-4 USD above last month. Domestically, SCG SG660/SP660 and local-plant PVC held stable at VND 23,700-24,200 incl VAT; other oil-based PVC 23,500-24,500. Coal-based: Yihua distributor offered SG-5 at Yen Vien (Hanoi) at VND 23,100/kg incl VAT (3-4 week delivery), down just VND 100 vs late September — coal-based PVC staying fairly stable.
